content:
In today's age of generative AI, creativity and code go hand-in-hand. What if you could generate stunning images with the flair of Van Gogh or the abstraction of Picasso — just by typing a sentence? In this blog post, we’ll walk you through how to build a web-based AI art generator using Python, Streamlit, and the OpenAI Image API.

💡 What You'll Build

A sleek app that:

  • Accepts a text prompt from the user
  • Lets users choose from 30+ famous art styles
  • Generates a custom image using AI
  • Allows downloading the result

🧰 Tech Stack

  • Python
  • Streamlit for UI
  • OpenAI API for image generation
  • Pillow for image handling
  • Requests and certifi for secure image fetching

🖼️ Full List of Supported Art Styles

Here are just a few examples of the styles you can generate:

  • Impressionist
  • Surrealist
  • Realism
  • Pop Art
  • Renaissance
  • Street Art
  • Hyperrealism
    …and many more!

In total, 35 diverse art movements are supported — offering endless creative combinations.

🚀 Code Breakdown

1. 🔐 Setup the OpenAI API Key

Make sure your OpenAI key is securely stored in a file called apikey.py:

from apikey import apikey

Then load it into your environment and initialize the OpenAI client:

import os
from openai import OpenAI
os.environ['OPENAI_API_KEY'] = apikey
OpenAI.api_key = apikey
client = OpenAI()

2. 🧠 UI with Streamlit

Streamlit helps us build the frontend in just a few lines:

import streamlit as st

st.title("AI Image Generator with Artistic Styles")
st.write("Enter a prompt and select an art style to generate an image.")

We then gather user input:

prompt = st.text_input("Enter the image prompt:", "A beautiful sunset over a calm sea")
style = st.selectbox("Select an art style:", art_styles)
size = st.selectbox("Select image size:", ["1024x1024", "512x512", "256x256"])

3. 🎨 Generate and Display Image

When the button is clicked, the app combines the prompt and style, then uses the OpenAI API to generate the image:

if st.button("Generate Image"):
    full_prompt = f"{prompt} in {style} style"
    response = client.images.generate(prompt=full_prompt, n=1, size=size)
    image_url = response.data[0].url

Then, we download and display it using Pillow:

img_response = requests.get(image_url, verify=certifi.where())
img = Image.open(BytesIO(img_response.content))
st.image(img, caption=f"Generated Image: {full_prompt}", use_column_width=True)

4. 💾 Add a Download Button

Let users download the generated image:

img_bytes = BytesIO()
img.save(img_bytes, format="PNG")
img_bytes.seek(0)
st.download_button(
    label="Download Image",
    data=img_bytes,
    file_name=f"{style.lower().replace(' ', '_')}.png",
    mime="image/png"
)

🧪 Try It Out

Once your script is ready, simply run:

streamlit run app.py

Visit the local URL in your browser and enjoy creating beautiful AI-powered images!

📦 Final Thoughts

This project is a fantastic blend of creativity and AI. Whether you're an artist, developer, or just curious, this app demonstrates how accessible and fun generative AI can be.

Feel free to extend the app by:

  • Adding more controls (brightness, contrast, filters)
  • Letting users input their own custom image dimensions
  • Saving image history in a gallery view

Let the machines paint your vision — one prompt at a time.

the full python code:

import os

import certifi
import streamlit as st
from openai import OpenAI
from apikey import apikey  # Store your OpenAI key in apikey.py
import requests
from PIL import Image
from io import BytesIO

# Set up the OpenAI API key
os.environ['OPENAI_API_KEY'] = apikey
OpenAI.api_key = apikey
client = OpenAI()

# List of art styles
art_styles = [
    "Impressionist", "Cubist", "Surrealist", "Realism", "Pop Art", "Abstract Expressionism",
    "Futurism", "Minimalism", "Baroque", "Romanticism", "Art Nouveau", "Dadaism", "Symbolism",
    "Neoclassicism", "Constructivism", "Renaissance", "Conceptual Art", "Post-Impressionism",
    "Expressionism", "Photorealism", "Op Art", "Bauhaus", "Street Art", "Suprematism",
    "Naïve Art", "Fauvism", "Hyperrealism", "Vorticism", "Rococo", "Lyrical Abstraction",
    "Precisionism", "De Stijl", "Tachisme", "Neo-Expressionism", "Art Deco"
]

# Streamlit UI setup
st.title("AI Image Generator with Artistic Styles")
st.write("Enter a prompt and select an art style to generate an image.")

# User input: Prompt and Art Style
prompt = st.text_input("Enter the image prompt:", "A beautiful sunset over a calm sea")
style = st.selectbox("Select an art style:", art_styles)
size = st.selectbox("Select image size:", ["1024x1024", "512x512", "256x256"])

if st.button("Generate Image"):
    # Generate image based on user input
    full_prompt = f"{prompt} in {style} style"
    st.write(f"Generating image for: '{full_prompt}'")

    response = client.images.generate(prompt=full_prompt, n=1, size=size)
    image_url = response.data[0].url

    # Fetch and display the image
    img_response = requests.get(image_url, verify=certifi.where())
    img = Image.open(BytesIO(img_response.content))

    st.image(img, caption=f"Generated Image: {full_prompt}", use_column_width=True)

    # Provide an option to download the image
    img_bytes = BytesIO()
    img.save(img_bytes, format="PNG")
    img_bytes.seek(0)
    st.download_button(label="Download Image", data=img_bytes, file_name=f"{style.lower().replace(' ', '_')}.png",
                       mime="image/png")
